title: A Compass for the Provision
premise: Yara Montrose, who has spent twelve years drifting between dig sites since her archaeologist father abandoned her, is drawn back to the coastal range when a winter storm exposes a sea cave matching a legend her father once dismissed as tourist bait. Inside she finds his field journal and a brass compass that points not north but toward something buried in the high passes — and evidence he went looking for it and never came out. Racing the first snows with a skeptical local guide and rivals from her father's old institute closing in, Yara must decide whether the inheritance she's chasing is treasure or an apology. She reaches the summit chamber ahead of her pursuers, finds her father's final letters, and chooses to leave the treasure buried, claiming instead the compass and the truth as her only inheritance.
about_author: Dominic Okonkwo is a former surveyor turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people mapping the distances inside themselves. He lives near the coast and still walks the tideline every morning, just in case.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps No Appointments
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working a routine coastal survey in the village of Penhallow, Yara watches a storm strip away a dune to reveal a cave mouth locals call the Provision. The emotional beat: restless competence masking grief; she measures everything in miles because years hurt too much.

chapters.title: Legends Charge Admission
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the village pub she hears the legend of the Provision — a cave that shows you what you're owed — and recognizes details from her father's old lectures. A local guide, Tomas Vey, warns her off. Beat: temptation versus self-protection.

chapters.title: What the Sea Gave Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At low tide she enters the cave alone and finds a sealed tin: her father Elias Montrose's field journal and a strange brass compass whose needle ignores north entirely. Beat: shock curdling into anger — he was here, within miles of her, and never sent word.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Yara's POV. Interleaved memories of the night Elias left, the digs they shared before it, and how she learned to outrun attachment. Beat: understanding that the compass isn't just pointing somewhere; it's pointing at her whole childhood.

chapters.title: The Needle That Lies
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, a former mountain rescue man with his own reasons for distrusting outsiders, examines the compass and grudgingly confirms its needle tracks something real — a magnetic anomaly deep in the range, mapped by his grandfather. Beat: reluctant alliance offered.

chapters.title: Rivals on the Road
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Two men from the Whitcombe Institute — her father's old employer — arrive asking questions about a missing 1998 expedition. Yara realizes she isn't the only one following the journal. Beat: paranoia; the race becomes literal.

chapters.title: Provisions
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Preparations in Penhallow: gear, mules, weather windows, and Tomas laying down hard rules. Yara signs on despite his warning that the passes close early this year. Beat: commitment — she chooses the mountain over the safe life.

chapters.title: First Ascent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The climb into the foothills; the compass needle steadies toward a named peak, Sarn Ddu. First journal excerpt reveals Elias believed the cave held a pre-Roman hoard — and that someone at the Institute wanted him silenced. Beat: purpose hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They shelter in a high hamlet where an old woman recognizes the compass as one of three made by a local smith generations ago. One other compass exists — and the Institute men carry it. Beat: dread; the past is closer than it seemed.

chapters.title: Weather Turning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An early storm forces them into a bothy for two days. Confined together, Yara and Tomas trade wounds: his failed rescue, her abandonment. Beat: intimacy through honesty; the miles between them begin to close.

chapters.title: The Journal's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reading further, she finds Elias's final entry breaks off mid-sentence above Sarn Ddu — and a folded letter addressed to her that he never sent. She can't bring herself to open it. Beat: the emotional core; grief refusing its delivery.

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Institute pair sabotage their cache at a river crossing, stealing supplies and the journal. Stranded and furious, Yara nearly turns back. Beat: lowest ebb; the quest stripped to will alone.

chapters.title: The Shepherd's Path
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Tomas leads them up an unmapped drover's road his grandfather used. The compass, deprived of the journal, becomes their only guide. Beat: trust tested and proven; dependence accepted.

chapters.title: Above the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Thin air, thin tempers. They spot the Institute men's camp below and must choose: confront or slip past. Yara chooses stealth, but overhears that the Institute believes Elias found the hoard alive and hid it. Beat: hope weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. First snow falls as they reach the saddle beneath Sarn Ddu. The compass needle spins wildly — then locks, pointing straight up. Whatever it seeks is overhead, not ahead. Beat: awe and vertigo; the map inverts.

chapters.title: The Other Compass
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Institute men catch up at the icefield. Standoff on the glacier; their leader, Dr. Renner, claims Elias stole Institute property. Tomas buys time with a bluff about the route. Beat: tension at breaking point; enemies forced into uneasy parallel pursuit.

chapters.title: Sarn Ddu
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climbing the final face in worsening snow, Yara realizes the 'cave' is a collapsed mine shaft behind the summit — and that Elias reached it. His rope anchors are still there, twelve years old. Beat: terror and tenderness side by side.

chapters.title: The Chamber of Owings
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Inside: not gold but a vault of the smith's making holding the region's lost records — debts forgiven, names restored, a community's true inheritance. And Elias's camp, his last letters, and proof he died protecting it from Renner's predecessor. Beat: revelation; the legend told the truth all along.

chapters.title: What You're Owed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cornered by Renner, who wants the site erased and claimed, Yara finally opens her father's letter — an apology without excuses. She triggers a controlled collapse, sealing the chamber and stranding Renner's claim. Beat: climax; she chooses memory over treasure, truth over profit.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The race down ahead of the full storm, Renner's party scattered, Yara carrying only the compass and the letter. Frostbite, exhaustion, and a rescue by the hamlet's shepherds. Beat: survival stripped bare; gratitude replacing grief.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Back in Penhallow, Yara gives her account to the villagers and a disbelieving Institute tribunal, backed by Tomas's grandfather's maps. Renner is discredited. Beat: justice without triumphalism; belonging earned rather than inherited.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Provision
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Spring. Yara stays in Penhallow, teaching local children to read the land, the cave sealed by mutual vow. The compass hangs on her wall, needle resting at last. Final beat: she stops measuring life in miles and starts measuring it in years — and finds she wants more of them.
